review_items.title: Chemours Fayetteville Works → DESCRIBED_BY → chemours-cd.pdf
review_items.detail: NER pulled The Chemours Company Fayetteville Works from the consent decree PDF and matched it to facility NCD844706749 on name + EPA ID. Any edge that crosses from an extracted document entity onto a ledger facility always sees a human — this is the edge the hero question ("what does the Chemours decree say, and are we accepting their waste?") rides on, so a wrong match is a wrong answer, not a cosmetic error.
evidence: extracted_entity=The Chemours Company Fayetteville Works; confidence=0.9

review_items.title: Stericycle Environmental Solutions — enforcement doc on a TRANSPORTER, not a generator
review_items.detail: Stericycle Environmental Solutions appears in the custody chain as a transporter (TRANSPORTS_TO VLS), and NER also linked it to a federal complaint + settlement. The document names the corporate entity; the graph holds the transporter handler. Attaching the enforcement to the hauling node is defensible but not certain — the complaint may concern a different Stericycle facility. A reviewer decides whether the DESCRIBED_BY edge attaches here.

review_items.title: Inbound-tonnage rollup mixes manifest tons with summary tons
review_items.detail: The SHIPS_TO.total_tons edge property is summed from e_manifest line quantities, while RCRA_Compliance_Summary carries a facility-level accepted-tonnage figure. They are close but not identical (rejected and residue manifests are treated differently). A measure that subtracts or compares the two is cross-basis and is never inferred — a human declares the basis or the validator blocks every use of it.
evidence: e_manifest rollup vs RCRA_Compliance_Summary accepted tonnage

review_items.title: Waste codes kept as a manifest attribute — promote to dimension nodes?
review_items.detail: Distinct WASTE CODE values (D/F/U/P series) are modelled as a multi-valued attribute on each Manifest, not as WasteCode nodes — a code carried on a row is an attribute of the shipment, not an entity with its own registry. 'Which generators send the most Land-Disposal-Restricted (LDR) waste?' still resolves, as a filter over that attribute. Promoting waste codes (or an LDR grouping) to dimension nodes is a modelling choice a reviewer may make for convenience, but the builder does not assume it — this is the correction to the earlier 'every column becomes a node' build.
evidence: waste_codes_seen rolled up on SHIPS_TO edges

review_items.title: Legacy generator name on 3 pre-2023 manifests — low-confidence SHIPS_TO match
review_items.detail: Three early manifests carry a generator name string that the fuzzy matcher tied to an EPA ID at 0.58 — below the 0.60 relationship floor. The name is a punctuation/spacing variant of an existing generator, but under the floor it does not auto-attach. Left unresolved, those three manifests' tonnage is orphaned from the generator's SHIPS_TO rollup.

pivot.title: Entity resolution: Texas Molecular LP vs VLS Texas Molecular
pivot.detail: Manifests shipped before 2023-01-05 carry Texas Molecular LP in DES FACILITY NAME; post-acquisition rows carry VLS Texas Molecular. Both resolve to EPA ID TXD000719518 via the alias table. Confidence is high, but an identity merge is never auto-applied — approving collapses the pre- and post-acquisition history onto one node and every rollup that cites either name inherits the merge.
pivot.why_pivot: Every inbound-flow row in this queue is measured against this facility’s history, so the queue cannot be read until the merge is settled.
evidence: entity_resolution: Texas Molecular LP -> FAC:TXD000719518 (alias table + EPA ID)

sanity_checks.question: What does the Chemours consent decree say, and are we accepting waste from that facility?
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The document node for chemours-cd.pdf is linked by DESCRIBED_BY to the Chemours Fayetteville Works facility, which is linked by SHIPS_TO to VLS Texas Molecular with tonnage and manifest count on the edge. Structured and unstructured data meet on one node — the traversal below is the whole point of the graph.
sanity_checks.plan: MATCH (d:Document {id:'DOC:chemours_cd'})<-[:DESCRIBED_BY]-(f:Facility)-[s:SHIPS_TO]->(vls:Facility {id:'FAC:TXD000719518'}) RETURN f, d, s.total_tons, s.manifests

sanity_checks.question: Trace manifest 346581037ELC cradle-to-grave: who generated it, who hauled it, when did we receive it?
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The manifest node carries GENERATED (from Arkema Crosby), TRANSPORTED (Sprint Waste Services, 5 days in possession) and RECEIVED_BY (VLS) edges. The chain is walkable node-by-node in custody order.
sanity_checks.plan: MATCH (gen:Facility)-[:GENERATED]->(m:Manifest {id:'MAN:346581037ELC'})-[:RECEIVED_BY]->(vls:Facility) MATCH (t:Facility)-[tr:TRANSPORTED]->(m) RETURN gen, t, tr.days, m, vls

sanity_checks.question: Which generators shipping to Deer Park are under active RCRA enforcement, and how much waste did we accept from them?
sanity_checks.verdict_body: Generator facilities carry ENFORCEMENT_AGAINST edges from Enforcement events and SHIPS_TO edges (manifests + tons) into VLS. The traversal joins the two so enforcement and accepted tonnage read on one path. Sub-graph shows three of the highest-exposure generators; the full query returns all 15.
sanity_checks.plan: MATCH (e:Enforcement)-[:ENFORCEMENT_AGAINST]->(f:Facility) MATCH (f)-[s:SHIPS_TO]->(vls:Facility {id:'FAC:TXD000719518'}) RETURN f, s.total_tons, s.manifests ORDER BY f.penalty_usd DESC

sanity_checks.question: Is 'Texas Molecular' the same facility as 'VLS Texas Molecular' — how does the system know?
sanity_checks.verdict_body: Three raw name strings resolve onto one facility node by alias table + EPA-ID match. The RESOLVES_TO sub-graph is the proof: the legacy pre-acquisition names and the current name all point at FAC:TXD000719518 with the method and confidence on each edge.

sanity_checks.question: Which generators send us the most Land-Disposal-Restricted (LDR) waste?
sanity_checks.verdict: Graph can answer this — LDR is a filter over a manifest attribute.
sanity_checks.verdict_body: Waste codes are a multi-valued attribute on each Manifest (and rolled up on the generator's SHIPS_TO edge), not WasteCode nodes. 'LDR' is a regulatory grouping of specific codes (D001, D008, D009, F-series...) applied as a filter over that attribute at query time — the same codes, no node to build. The traversal walks generator -> SHIPS_TO -> VLS and reads waste_codes_seen; per-manifest tonnage refines it. This is the corrected model: a code carried on a row is an attribute of the shipment, not an entity.
